dash.title: Talent strategy dashboard
dash.subtitleHr: {{cycle}} · Retention, succession and development of key talent across the plant
dash.scopeNoteManager: Covers your team and your line; Supervisors below you count only once they have submitted.
dash.noData: No data in the current scope.

completion.def: Key talent reviews already submitted to HR (including confirmed and locked).
completion.formula: Key talent submitted or later ÷ all key talent
completion.use: If it lags, open Review progress to see which teams have not submitted. Other measures are only representative once completion is high.
probe: Which teams have not started, and where are they stuck: choosing, writing, or not knowing how?
Is the submitted content good enough to make decisions on?
What help do Supervisors need before the deadline: one-to-one support or examples?

key.def: People a Supervisor marked as key talent this cycle.
key.formula: Number of key talent; share = key talent ÷ people in scope
key.use: The share is a reference, never a target. Use it to check that departments nominate consistently and raise outliers in calibration.
probe: Do departments nominate key talent on the same criteria? Can they say why this person?
Is anyone listed for seniority or goodwill rather than impact?
Who should be listed but is not, such as a fast-growing new hire?

alert.def: People in a critical role who are rated high retention risk.
alert.formula: Critical role = yes and retention risk = High
alert.use: Losing them hits the business immediately. Agree an individual retention action with the Supervisor and HRBP within two weeks.
probe: When did their Supervisor last talk with them about their career?
If they left next month, what would stop immediately, and who could step in?
What reason to stay can we offer: challenge, growth, recognition or pay?

ready.def: Share of critical roles with at least one successor who could step in now.
ready.formula: Critical roles with a Ready Now successor ÷ all critical roles
ready.use: Low coverage means an opening is likely filled from outside or stays vacant. Start with the Succession gaps list.
probe: For roles with low coverage, is there no candidate, or is the candidate one step away?
Do the ready-now successors know it, and do they want the role?
What single experience would bring a 1–2 year successor forward?

talk.def: Key talent whose Supervisor ticked 'career goals not yet discussed'.
talk.use: A 15-minute career conversation is the cheapest retention action. Start with medium and high risk.
probe: Why has the conversation not happened: not knowing how to start, or no time?
What would help Supervisors hold it well: a question list, an example, or an HRBP alongside?
Where should the outcome go: the development plan or a retention action?

health.def: Four core measures per department, compared with the overall value of the current filter.
health.formula: Flagged when 10 or more points worse than overall.
health.use: Start with the department with the most flags, then open the other sections for the reasons. This compares departments, not Supervisors.
probe: In the department with most flags, is the issue shared or concentrated in one team?
Is the department leader aware of this picture?
Which cell do we want to change by the next review?

headcount.t: Headcount and key talent by department
headcount.def: People in review scope per department and how many of them are key talent.
headcount.formula: Dark = key talent; light = others in scope; percentage = key talent ÷ people in scope
headcount.use: Check whether key talent sits in a few departments. Clear differences in share are worth a consistency check.
probe: Where the key talent share is high, are criteria looser? Where it is low, is anyone missed?
How exposed is a department whose key talent is concentrated?
Large departments with few key talent: is it the nature of the work, or under-development?

gender.q: At which step does the share of women drop?
gender.def: Share of women at each step: review scope, key talent, critical roles, ready now.
gender.formula: Women at each step ÷ people at that step; hidden under five
gender.use: The step with the clear drop is where to check nomination, appointment or development opportunities.
probe: At which step does the share of women drop: nomination, critical roles, or readiness?
Do our criteria disadvantage some ways of working?
At the biggest drop, what can we do: mentoring, rotation, or clearer criteria?

tenure.q: At what career stage is our key talent?
tenure.def: Share of key talent and of everyone in scope in each tenure band.
tenure.formula: People in each band ÷ people in that group
tenure.use: Skewed senior: knowledge-transfer and retirement risk. Skewed junior: more coaching needed.
probe: Is senior key talent passing on their experience in a planned way?
Does junior key talent have enough coaching and stage?
What will this picture look like in five years, and are we ready?

riskMap.def: Key talent split by retention risk (high, medium, low) and by whether they hold a critical role.
riskMap.formula: Each cell = number of people; click for the list
riskMap.use: Handle high risk × critical role first, then medium risk × critical role.
probe: Does every high-risk critical person have an owner and a date?
For medium risk, what moved them up from low?
Are we taking the low-risk but very critical people for granted?

reasons.def: Reasons Supervisors ticked for medium and high risk people (several allowed).
reasons.formula: People with the reason ÷ medium and high risk people
reasons.use: When reasons cluster, a policy fix (pay, career paths, workload) beats one-by-one retention.
probe: Can a policy fix the most common reason, or does it need one-by-one action?
Are these reasons the Supervisor's guess, or what the person said?
If we could fix only one reason first, which has most impact?

poach.def: High retention risk and already ready for their next role.
poach.formula: Retention risk = High and next-role readiness = Ready Now
poach.use: Ready but without an opportunity. Discuss promotion, rotation or a bigger scope first.
probe: Do they know we see them as ready?
Is there a real opportunity in the next six months?
If not, can a bigger scope or project keep them for now?

talkRisk.q: Who should we talk to this week?
talkRisk.def: Medium or high retention risk, and the Supervisor has not discussed career goals with them.
talkRisk.formula: Retention risk = Medium or High, and 'not yet discussed' ticked
talkRisk.use: Hold a 15-minute career conversation within two weeks.
probe: Who books this conversation, and by when?
Is the Supervisor ready to hear "I want to leave"?
Who follows up that promises made are kept?

benchDept.q: If a critical role opened tomorrow, who would step in?
benchDept.def: Each critical role, grouped by the readiness of its best successor.
benchDept.formula: Ready now; 1–2 years; long-range = 3+ years or emergency cover only; none = no successor or to be hired (TBH)
benchDept.use: Red roles have nobody today. Amber plus red is the two-year succession gap.
probe: Red roles: is nobody available, or has nobody looked yet?
Amber candidates: which experience do they lack most?
Blue candidates: is acting-up or rotation planned for the coming year?

uncovered.q: Which critical roles have nobody within two years?
uncovered.def: Critical roles where no successor could take over within two years (long-range, emergency cover, TBH or none).
uncovered.formula: Critical role and best successor is 3+ years, emergency cover or none
uncovered.use: Name a successor first; where nobody exists internally, plan hiring early.
probe: Which of these roles would hurt most if it opened?
Could someone from another department be a candidate?
For roles needing an outside hire, has recruiting been told?

concentration.q: Is someone the backup for several roles?
concentration.def: The same person named as successor for two or more critical roles.
concentration.formula: Roles per named successor, two or more only
concentration.use: One person can fill only one role, so real coverage is lower than it looks. Find a second candidate. HR only.
probe: Can they really back up this many roles at once?
If they take one role, who covers the rest?
Can each of these roles find another candidate?

external.def: Share of successor slots that are external candidates or to be hired (TBH).
external.formula: External and TBH ÷ all successor slots
external.use: Higher means more reliance on hiring and more room to grow internal talent.
probe: Are these roles external because nobody is inside, or because nobody is being developed?
Have we estimated the time and cost of hiring?
Which role could start growing an internal candidate now?

fragile.def: The near-term successor (ready now or 1–2 years) of a critical role is themselves at medium or high risk.
fragile.formula: Near-term successor with retention risk Medium or High
fragile.use: Both could leave together. Retaining the successor protects two roles.
probe: What is the successor's own retention action?
Do holder and successor share a team and the same reasons to leave?
Do we need a second candidate?

pipeline.q: How many are ready to step up?
pipeline.def: Readiness of key talent for their next role. With several next roles, the nearest counts.
pipeline.formula: People at each readiness ÷ key talent with a next role
pipeline.use: Ready people without an opportunity become a retention risk.
probe: Do ready people have a real opportunity in the coming year?
What experience do 1–2 year people lack most?
For 3+ years, does the current plan shorten the time enough?

mobility.def: Key talent's openness to moving to another department, site or location.
mobility.formula: People per option ÷ key talent who answered
mobility.use: People open to moving soon are the first internal source for openings.
probe: Where do those open to moving want to go, and why?
For "not now": family reasons, or no attractive opportunity?
Will these people hear first when an internal role opens?

mix.q: Do plans build skills on the job, or only in class?
mix.def: Actual share of development actions by type, against the 70/20/10 reference.
mix.formula: Actions of each type ÷ actions with a type
mix.use: A high share of courses (10%) means plans lack real assignments. The reference is not a target.
probe: How many real on-the-job assignments are in the plans?
After a course, is there a chance to apply what was learned?
Do mentoring and benchmarking have a named partner and rhythm?

checkpoints.def: Development goals falling due in each month.
checkpoints.use: A month before a peak, HR reminds Supervisors to prepare follow-ups.
probe: Do Supervisors have time to follow up in peak months?
Who reminds, and who confirms?
How do results feed the next review?

pbm.q: What are our common strengths and gaps?
pbm.def: How often each Our Values item was named as a strength and as an improvement area.
pbm.formula: Mentions per value (left: improvement, right: strength)
pbm.use: Improvement areas many people share are good topics for a group workshop.
probe: Is the most common improvement area personal, or caused by the environment?
Are the most common strengths used and recognized?
Which topic most deserves a group workshop first?

planComplete.def: Share of key talent whose development plan has every required field.
planComplete.formula: Key talent with a complete plan ÷ all key talent
planComplete.use: Incomplete plans cannot be tracked. Ask Supervisors to add actions, dates and how progress is checked.
probe: Which field is most often missing?
Do Supervisors not know how to write it, or lack time?
What example or template can we provide?

keyReasons.def: Reasons Supervisors chose for each key talent (several allowed).
keyReasons.formula: People with the reason ÷ key talent
keyReasons.use: The mix shows what the organization really depends on. Many scarce-skill holders mean transfer risk; many high-potential people need development resources.
probe: Do the reasons people are key match the capabilities the department will need?
Is anyone learning the scarce skills yet?
Does every high-potential person have a development plan to match?

roleMatrix.q: Which roles may open with nobody ready?
roleMatrix.def: Each critical role placed by the holder's retention risk and the readiness of the best successor. Roles are compared, not people.
roleMatrix.formula: Across: holder retention risk (high, medium, low). Down: successor (none, long-range, 1–2 years, ready now)
roleMatrix.use: Act on the top-right first (high risk, nobody ready), then work outward.
probe: Top-right roles: the holder may leave and nobody is ready. Who owns it, and by when?
Do several roles in one department sit in the danger zone?
Retain the holder first or build the successor first: which is faster?

depth.q: How many candidates does each critical role have?
depth.def: Named successor candidates per critical role (internal or external, TBH excluded).
depth.use: One candidate is fragile: if they leave, coverage is gone. Common practice is at least two for critical roles.
probe: If the only successor also leaves, what then?
Could another team provide a second candidate?
Where there are two or more, do the candidates know their paths?

pool.q: When a role opens, who inside should we talk to first?
pool.def: Key talent ready for a next role within two years and open to moving within two years.
pool.formula: Mobility = now or 1–2 years, and next-role readiness = ready now or 1–2 years
pool.use: Start here when a role opens. A small pool means weak internal mobility.
probe: Are these people matched to specific openings or successor slots?
Will their Supervisors let them go?
Is internal transfer fast enough that they do not leave while waiting?

planExec.def: Current status of every development goal.
planExec.formula: Goals per status (people = those holding a goal in that status)
planExec.use: Find the cause of at-risk and not-started goals before the next checkpoint. Development happens in execution, after the review.
probe: At-risk plans: blocked by time, resources, or Supervisor support?
Why have not-started plans not started?
Did completed plans change anything visible?

story.title: What stands out
story.subtitle: Built automatically from the current filter. Every number opens the list.
story.none: Nothing stands out in the current scope.
story.riskHotspot: {{pct}} of key talent in {{dept}} is at medium or high risk, well above overall ({{overall}}).
story.riskHotspotAct: Next: review the reasons with that department's Supervisors
story.uncovered: {{count}} of {{critical}} critical roles have nobody who could take over within two years.
story.uncoveredAct: Next: name successors or plan hiring early
story.concentration: {{name}} is named successor for {{roles}} roles, so real coverage is lower than it looks.
story.concentrationAct: Next: find a second candidate for those roles
story.talkGap: {{count}} people at medium or high risk have not had a career conversation.
story.talkGapAct: Next: hold a 15-minute career conversation within two weeks

org.tenureHint: Hover a bar for headcount; click it to open the list

bench.noConcentration: Nobody is named for more than one role.

act.title: Action list
act.subtitle: Turns the review into this month's to-dos. Each item is a conversation to have, not a judgement of anyone. Cross-team results are HR only.

talk.why: Medium or high risk, and nobody has discussed their career with them.
talk.next: Supervisor holds a 15-minute conversation within two weeks

fragile.why: The successor may leave too, opening two roles at once.
fragile.next: Add the successor to retention actions, or name a second candidate

hidden.t: Check potential that may be missed
hidden.why: Other Supervisors see them as a near-term successor, but their own Supervisor did not list them as key talent.
hidden.next: Confirm in calibration whether to add them

internal.why: These roles lack successors, and someone's stated next step is exactly this job.
internal.next: Talk to these colleagues before opening the role

calibrate.t: Ask one more question in calibration
calibrate.why: These teams' entries follow a pattern (all low risk, identical readiness) worth confirming.
calibrate.next: HRBP checks the basis for the entries in the discussion

act.none: Nothing to act on right now.

riskNoPlan.why: Medium or high risk, but the development plan is incomplete. Keeping people needs a direction to grow.
riskNoPlan.next: Write the retention conversation into the development plan

dash.probeTitle: Questions to ask in the discussion
dash.pipeFlat: The share of women is similar at every step
dash.pipeHeadline: Women are {{scope}} of review scope and {{end}} at "{{last}}"
dash.deptGap: By department: scope vs. key talent
dash.deptGapNote: Gray dot = women in scope, violet dot = women among key talent. A red line means 5+ points fewer among key talent.
dash.matrixNone: No critical role is in the danger zone.
dash.depthTake: {{pct}} of critical roles have fewer than two candidates
dash.poolTake: {{count}} key talent are ready and open to moving within two years
dash.convPrepNote: Generated from what the Supervisor entered. Questions to ask, not conclusions.

person.aspirations: "What do you most want to achieve at work in the next year or two, and how can I help?"
person.riskNoReason: "Is anything at work making you feel stuck or wanting a change?"
person.readyNow: "If you had the chance to take on {{role}}, would you want it? What would you still need?"
person.noSuccessor: (Ask yourself) "If they were away for a month from tomorrow, what would stop, and who could start learning it?"
person.mobileNow: "Where would you like to go next, and what matters most to you?"
person.plan: "Let's make the development goal concrete: what will be different when it is done, and who confirms it?"
person.planAtRisk: "Where is the plan stuck? What should I change: time, resources, or opportunities?"

reason.Career Move: "What would you like to be doing in two years, and what step is missing now?"
reason.Competitive Market: "What attracts you about outside offers, and which of those could we offer here?"
reason.Family Reasons: "Is there a work arrangement that would make things easier at home?"
reason.Compensation Reasons: "Do you feel your reward matches your contribution? Which part matters most to you?"
reason.Retirement: "What are your plans for the next few years, and how would you like to pass on your experience?"
reason.Hybrid Work: "What way of working lets you do your best?"
reason.Work Environment: "What in the team makes the work harder than it should be?"
reason.Risk of burnout: "Is your current workload sustainable? What could we set aside?"
reason.Role Development/Role Fit: "Which parts of your role give you the most satisfaction, and which would you like less of?"
reason.Culture Fit: "What here feels different from the way you like to work?"
